about: Every experiment the articles state, for the platform's experiments page (migration 0023). `SequencePlatform.Ingest publish-experiments` publishes each entry with its CSVs from this folder as an 'article' run. runnable: can be rerun from the database alone; experiments that need DNA never can. commit: the last commit that changed the CSVs. Numbers are those in README.md. The P9 runs with findings (e1-outliers, e1b-outliers-cvtree, e2b-phage-host, e4-cpg) are published by their own scripts with --publish and are not listed here.

experiments.name: build-time
experiments.title: Profile build time
experiments.question: How fast is a windowed Z-curve profile built, from 20 kbp to 10.24 Mbp?
experiments.note: Timed in a Debug build; A4 reruns it in Release.

experiments.name: compare-time
experiments.title: Whole-sequence compare time
experiments.question: How long does comparing two whole profiles take?
experiments.note: Debug build (A4).

experiments.name: localization-time
experiments.title: Fragment localization time
experiments.question: How long does BestAlignment take to place a fragment in a long sequence?
experiments.note: Debug build (A4).

experiments.name: reliability-at-scale
experiments.title: Score against known mutation rate
experiments.question: Does the score fall steadily with the substitution rate, at every length?
experiments.note: Substitutions only; indels are planned (A10). 5 seeds per length.

experiments.name: nw-accuracy
experiments.title: Accuracy against Needleman–Wunsch
experiments.question: How does the score track global alignment identity from 500 bp to 20 kbp?

experiments.name: genome-scale
experiments.title: A 3.1 Gbp genome, streamed
experiments.question: Can a human-sized genome be profiled, searched and stored without loading it as a string?
experiments.note: The compare and reliability rows predate the SIMD rewrite (upper bounds).

keyNumbers.label: ms to find a planted fragment

experiments.name: distance-matrix
experiments.title: 30 bacteria, all pairs
experiments.question: Do scores order pairs by relationship: same species, genus, phylum, different phylum?

experiments.name: external-baseline
experiments.title: Against Mash and FastANI
experiments.question: How do the scores relate to Mash and FastANI on the same 435 pairs?
experiments.note: Mash saturates for distant pairs while the Z-curve stays graded; FastANI returns nothing for most pairs. Mash and FastANI outputs are in results/raw/.

keyNumbers.label: Pearson r with Mash, 22 pairs above its floor

experiments.name: retrieval-classification
experiments.title: Retrieval against Mash
experiments.question: Ranking pairs by score, how well are same-genus and same-phylum pairs found, against Mash?
experiments.note: Mash ranks better.

experiments.name: window-size
experiments.title: Window size sensitivity
experiments.question: How do 250, 500, 1,000 and 2,000 bp windows change the relationship levels?

experiments.name: single-point-ceiling
experiments.title: The single-point ceiling (CAT)
experiments.question: Does a single-point profile tell phiX174 from lambda phage?
experiments.note: CAT was removed from the code; it is at commit e152aa4.
experiments.command: git checkout e152aa4, then the phage motivating example in SequenceAnaliseTests

experiments.name: windowing-strategy
experiments.title: Fixed window size, not fixed count
experiments.question: Does a fixed window size keep unrelated pairs from drifting together as sequences grow?

experiments.name: window-count
experiments.title: Window count decides quality
experiments.question: How few windows can the shorter genome keep before retrieval suffers?
experiments.note: Bacteria lose no AUC down to a median of about 4 windows; with 0 windows Compare returns 0.

experiments.name: ladder
experiments.title: The multi-resolution ladder
experiments.question: Comparing at the coarsest level that keeps 8 windows: same accuracy, less time?
experiments.note: All pairs in 8.6 ms instead of 23.5 s.

experiments.name: gc-baseline
experiments.title: GC alone as a baseline
experiments.question: How close does GC content alone get to the Z-curve's retrieval?
experiments.note: The genus AUC rests on 8 positive pairs (CI about ±0.17).

experiments.name: gc-stratum
experiments.title: Beyond GC, on same-GC pairs
experiments.question: On pairs of nearly equal GC, does the score still separate taxa?
experiments.note: 437 catalogue genomes. All pairs: Spearman 0.993 between 1 − Compare and |ΔGC|. Same-GC pairs: ties GC at genus, beats it at family (+0.074) and phylum (+0.10 to +0.14).

experiments.name: strand-rotation
experiments.title: Strand and rotation
experiments.question: Does a genome against its own reverse complement or rotation still look identical?
experiments.note: It scores like a different strain: the query is compared on both strands since.

keyNumbers.label: K-12 vs itself rotated by half

experiments.name: origin-rotation
experiments.title: Replication origin from the profile
experiments.question: Does the minimum of the cumulative GC skew find the origin, and does rotating there restore identity?

keyNumbers.label: K-12 vs itself rotated, as stored (32 kbp)

experiments.name: genome-moments
experiments.title: Moments on genome windows
experiments.question: Do Legendre moments help on the unanchored genome ladder, as they do on genes?
experiments.note: Retrieval unchanged (0.830 / 0.794); arbitrary-phase localization drops. The genome ladder keeps means.

experiments.name: catalogue-localization
experiments.title: Localizing fragments over the catalogue
experiments.question: Is a fragment's source found among all records, at the coarsest level leaving 4 windows?
experiments.note: Source in the top 100 in 30/30 at 10–200 kbp, 23–26/30 at 4 kbp. Cached 0.17–1.14 s per fragment.

experiments.name: localization-validation
experiments.title: True start of real fragments
experiments.question: Are 2, 10 and 50 kbp fragments of real genomes placed at their true start, on both strands?
experiments.note: 40/40 at 10 and 50 kbp; 14/20 at 2 kbp inside a named record.

experiments.name: somatic-mutations
experiments.title: Somatic point mutations
experiments.question: Can the score see tumour-like point mutations between two copies of a genome?
experiments.note: 100 per Mbp move the score 9–620× less than the closest strain pair.

keyNumbers.label: score change at 100 mutations per Mbp

experiments.name: back-translation
experiments.title: Protein search by back-translation
experiments.question: Can a back-translated protein be localized in genome windows?
experiments.note: No-go: genome windows reach at most 3.3% top-1; per-gene profiles pooled over 30 bacteria at most 42.5%.

experiments.name: cds-sweep
experiments.title: The gene profile
experiments.question: Which per-gene profile finds a gene from its protein alone?
experiments.note: Adopted: codon positions 1 and 2, windows of 500 bp of gene from the start codon, Legendre moments P0–P2 of x, y, z. Means alone reach 50.2%.

experiments.name: cds-precision
experiments.title: 16-bit gene profiles
experiments.question: Can the gene profile be stored in 16 or 8 bits without losing search accuracy?
experiments.note: 16-bit halves change no number (largest difference 0.0001); 8-bit costs 1.8–5.9 points.

experiments.name: short-proteins
experiments.title: Proteins of 50–499 aa
experiments.question: Do 5 equal windows, compared within ±10% of the length, find short genes and their orthologs?
experiments.note: Orthologs 84–90%.

experiments.name: under-50-aa
experiments.title: Proteins under 50 aa
experiments.question: Does the short-gene rule work for 20–49 aa?
experiments.note: Passes, not built (needs a BV-BRC re-download).

experiments.name: protein-catalogue
experiments.title: Protein search over the catalogue
experiments.question: From the protein alone, is the right gene first among 64.3M genes?
experiments.note: 301 proteins. The file's 'family top-1 100%' counts the query's own gene; protein-homolog gives it without. Runnable once its query set is stored.

experiments.name: protein-homolog
experiments.title: Right family without the query's own gene
experiments.question: Is the right protein family first once the query's own gene, genome, species or genus is removed?
experiments.rule: Under 50% family top-1 with the own species removed in any band reframes the claim as near-identical lookup. No band was under 50%.
experiments.note: 157 proteins with a PGfam. Runnable once its query set is stored.

experiments.name: protein-family-tuning
experiments.title: Raising the right family
experiments.question: Do feature weights or a vote over the top hits find the right family more often, with the own genus removed?
experiments.rule: The combination best on the tuning half must gain ≥ 5 points on the test half, 95% genome-bootstrap CI excluding 0, losing ≤ 1 point of exact top-1. Best was 'best hit with a family': +3.1 points (paired CI +1.6 to +5.0; the first run printed −8.7 to +15.3 from an unpaired-bootstrap bug, fixed 2026-11-20). Below +5, so tuning stops.
experiments.note: 1,143 proteins from 64 genomes. Not pre-registered: 1/variance weights raise exact-gene top-1 on the test half from 83.7% to 87.8%. Runnable once its query set is stored.

experiments.name: protein-weights
experiments.title: Weighted gene-profile score
experiments.question: On genomes no earlier run used, do fixed 1/variance weights on the 9 numbers find the query's own gene first more often?
experiments.rule: Exact-gene top-1 must gain ≥ 2 points with the 95% genome-bootstrap CI above 0, losing ≤ 1 point of family top-1. Gain +1.3 points (CI +0.4 to +2.3), family −0.5: below the bar.
experiments.note: 1,268 proteins from 57 new genomes (seed 20261113). Adopted anyway on 2026-11-20 by the author's decision, for accuracy: the gain is small but its CI is above 0, and the earlier run gave +4.1. The platform scores weighted since then (protein null version 2).

keyNumbers.label: family top-1, own genus removed, weighted

experiments.name: protein-exact-miss
experiments.title: Why the own gene is not first
experiments.question: When the query's own gene is not first, what is?
experiments.rule: If identical or near-identical proteins are at least half of the misses, report 'right protein first' beside 'own gene first'. 164 of 193 (85%).
experiments.note: 1,143 proteins. The gene ranked above the own gene is mostly the same protein in a sister genome; partial genes explain 3 of 87 misses at 500+ aa. Ties are counted for the own gene; the API breaks them by record id.

experiments.name: protein-homolog-key
experiments.title: Family label or real homolog
experiments.question: Is the top hit a real homolog, and are the family 'misses' partly label noise?
experiments.rule: If the same-family gene is not detectably homologous in ≥ 10 points more of misses than of hits, CI above 0, the paper may say misses are partly label noise. 17.8% vs 0.9%: +16.9 points (CI +12.1 to +21.4).
experiments.note: 989 proteins with a same-family gene outside their genus, weighted score. Homolog: Rost's HSSP curve + 5 points over ≥ 60% of the shorter protein (BLOSUM62, gap 11 + k). The low identity bins are optimistic by construction.

experiments.name: protein-offset
experiments.title: Shifted same-family profiles
experiments.question: Are missed same-family genes the right profile at an offset?
experiments.rule: Flips ≥ 30% with most within 10 aa of the alignment's offset leads to a ranking test (protein-homolog-ranking). 47.8%, 82% within 10 aa: tested there.
experiments.note: 341 misses with both proteins from BV-BRC. True pairs are distant homologs (median identity 48%, inner indels in 77%); a shift mostly repairs P1 and P2.

keyNumbers.label: true beats wrong at best offsets

experiments.name: protein-homolog-ranking
experiments.title: Translation-built genes and offset search
experiments.question: Does profiling genes from their translation, or searching over shifts, rank homologs first more often?
experiments.rule: Either arm must gain ≥ 3 points of homolog top-1 with the CI above 0. Translation +1.9 (CI −1.9 to +5.1); shifts −6.0 (CI −11.2 to −0.9). Neither: both dropped.
experiments.note: 300 proteins from the 30 bundled bacteria, 215 with a homolog in another genus. Homolog first by identity: 13% under 40%, 32% at 40–60%, 83% at 60–80%, 98% above.

experiments.name: protein-null
experiments.title: p and E for protein hits
experiments.question: How often does a gene of another family score this high against a protein of this length?
experiments.note: From 411 real proteins scored against genes of other families. Rebuilt for the weighted score on 2026-11-20 (version 2).

experiments.name: eukaryote-genes
experiments.title: Eukaryote genes from CDS files
experiments.question: Does protein search find eukaryote genes built from their CDS files?
experiments.note: 131 annotated assemblies, 2.25M genes, 209 MB. Yeast 100%.

experiments.name: gene-match
experiments.title: Reciprocal best genes without a family
experiments.question: Does the gene score alone pair genes with their counterparts in another genome?
experiments.note: Against 0.5% and 0.2% by chance.

experiments.name: search-breakdown
experiments.title: Where a protein search spends its time
experiments.question: Reading, decoding or scoring: what dominates a protein search, and what cut it?
experiments.note: Pooled buffers and scoring in place cut the time above the transfer floor by 58%; PostgreSQL's transfer is now 74–92% of a query.

experiments.name: bulk-load
experiments.title: The bulk load
experiments.question: How long does filling the catalogue from BV-BRC take, and how many duplicates are there?
experiments.note: 19,964 stored, 1,982 duplicates skipped (12.6% of viruses), 0 failed; 8.6 h active.
experiments.command: dotnet run --project SequencePlatform.Ingest -- ingest-bvbrc --group bacteria --limit N

experiments.name: neighbour-ranking
experiments.title: Re-ranking by shared neighbours
experiments.question: Does re-ranking the top 100 by shared top-20 neighbours find more same-genus genomes?
experiments.note: Bacteria p = 0.002; viruses 0.462 → 0.491.

experiments.name: rotation-production
experiments.title: Origin rotation in find-similar
experiments.question: Does scoring circular chromosomes from their origin find more same-genus genomes?
experiments.note: Warm E. coli search 76 → 382 ms.

experiments.name: wrap-around
experiments.title: Circularly permuted viruses
experiments.question: Does scoring a virus candidate wrapped around its end find more same-genus viruses?
experiments.note: 1.15× the time. Skipping neighbour re-ranking for viruses was checked and not taken.

keyNumbers.label: AUC same genus vs other family, before

experiments.name: second-order
experiments.title: The second-order Z-curve equals Karlin ρ*
experiments.question: Do Z-curve means and lag-1 covariances rebuild the dinucleotide signature exactly?
experiments.note: log ρ* in Z-curve axes is a rotation: same trees, map |r| = 1.000000. Dropping the 7 neighbour coefficients is what made the incomplete form trail.

experiments.name: relatives
experiments.title: Nearest relatives
experiments.question: Are a genome's 10 nearest signatures its relatives?
experiments.note: 4–9 ms per query.

keyNumbers.label: E. coli K-12: Escherichia/Shigella in its 10

experiments.name: e2-phage-host
experiments.title: Phage host from the signature (round 1)
experiments.question: Does the dinucleotide signature or localization tell a phage's host genus?
experiments.note: Weak pass against GC, but always guessing Escherichia gives 0.110. Localization: 0/200. Round 2 (e2b, 6-mers) passes.

experiments.name: e3-islands
experiments.title: Genomic islands
experiments.question: Do windows that deviate from their genome mark genomic islands better than GC?

experiments.name: e5-habitat
experiments.title: Habitat beyond genus and GC
experiments.question: Do signature neighbours share a habitat more than a within-genus shuffle predicts?
experiments.note: 82 of 108 genera above the shuffle, p = 3·10⁻⁸.

experiments.name: insert-check
experiments.title: Inserts between two genomes
experiments.question: Can two genomes' profiles show what one has that the other lacks?
experiments.note: Rule: ≥ 80% of inserts ≥ 10 kbp at ≤ 1 false call per Mbp. Same-GC donors are missed.

experiments.name: kmer-check
experiments.title: Longer k-mers for phage hosts
experiments.question: Do 3- to 6-mers tell a phage's host better than dinucleotides?
experiments.note: 207 phages and hosts streamed from NCBI and counted without keeping DNA. Led to storing 6-mer counts.
